statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of seven public paths. Not covered: authenticated account settings, payment/subscription flows, playback after media start, personalized signed-in states, and every BBC product subdomain; these require credentials or represent separate product templates.

page.framework: React-like server-rendered MPA with legacy and modern product surfaces
page.notes: Large public-service publishing ecosystem. Homepage and article raw HTML retain 97–99% of rendered content. Dynamic headlines reflect the live site at capture time.

checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten menu open/escape cycles, the heap summary grew from 689,702 nodes / 38.9 MB self-size to 887,218 nodes / 52.2 MB. Separate page processes add noise, so this is a low-confidence leak signal, not a proven retained path.
Baseline heap is 38.9 MB self-size for a very large media homepage; substantial but proportionate to the 100-image, component-rich page, with the interaction growth separately flagged.
Heap summaries do not surface Detached* among the top constructors; growth remains a low-confidence general signal handled by BBC-015 rather than proof of detached DOM/listener accumulation.

findings.summary: The public homepage remains light when the system requests a dark colour scheme.
findings.evidence: The prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshot is visually identical to the light capture; the probe reports color-scheme "normal" and body background rgb(248, 248, 248).
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, border and image treatments using the dark-mode guidance.

findings.summary: Long-running animations continue under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
findings.evidence: The emulated reduced-motion probe found sixteen running animations named animation-w6tfot, each with an 8,000 ms duration.
findings.suggestedFix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove non-essential looping animation and stop auto-advance while preserving essential state feedback.

findings.summary: State and route changes do not expose View Transition styling.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero authored view-transition rules across accessible stylesheets on an interaction-rich homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for major route and state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: First-visit overlays substantially obscure primary content on mobile.
findings.evidence: Mobile captures show the fixed cookie banner occupying roughly the lower 40% of the viewport across templates; the article capture also shows a centered sign-in promotion layered above both article and cookie banner.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the consent surface to the minimum legally required footprint and delay the optional personalization prompt until an explicit user action; ensure clear light-dismiss where appropriate.

findings.summary: Modal experiences are implemented as generic divs with ARIA rather than native dialog primitives.
findings.evidence: The overlay DOM probe found three DIV elements with role=dialog and aria-modal=true; no native dialog or popover elements were found on the representative news template.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native <dialog> for modal media flows and popover for transient non-modal UI, retaining accessible names and declarative dismissal.

findings.summary: Mobile lab loading and main-thread responsiveness miss the good performance range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.7 s, TBT 1,350 ms, max potential FID 740 ms, and a performance score of 0.64; the trace independently recorded 309 ms TBT and a 189 ms longest task.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP dependency and interaction tasks, prioritize the LCP image, and split or defer long JavaScript work using the performance guidance.

findings.summary: Large script execution tasks block the main thread.
findings.evidence: Trace evidence contains three long tasks (189, 182, and 88 ms); Lighthouse reports 1,350 ms total blocking time and 14.3 s time to interactive.
findings.suggestedFix: Break long work into schedulable chunks, defer below-fold component hydration, and remove unnecessary startup execution.

findings.summary: The homepage has a broad startup dependency and script payload.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 97 requests and 1.40 MB transferred, including 67 scripts (698 KB); several high-priority parser-initiated bundles were listed, while DOM confirmation shows the core bundles are async modules, so the issue is breadth and cost rather than a claim that those modules block parsing.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce initial component bundles, defer non-critical features and analytics, and preserve explicit LCP image priority.

findings.summary: Chrome reports browser inspector issues on load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse best-practices scored 0.77 and the inspector-issues audit failed, despite the document otherwise using a valid doctype and charset.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the concrete DevTools Issues-panel entries and add regression monitoring for browser deprecations and policy issues.

findings.summary: Tracking and analytics requests run on a first visit while the banner says additional cookies are off by default.
findings.evidence: The tracker capture observed 16 non-page origins and an active scorecardresearch tracker; the HAR attributes 95 of 97 requests and 1.28 MB to origins other than www.bbc.co.uk (including BBC-owned CDNs), and cookies include long-lived Chartbeat/analytics identifiers.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential measurement until affirmative consent, minimize identifiers and retention, batch essential analytics, and document why every pre-consent endpoint is necessary.

findings.summary: The sign-in entry offers username/password or Google but no phishing-resistant passkey path.
findings.evidence: The live sign-in probe found a username form with correct autocomplete and no passkey or PublicKeyCredential affordance; the page text offers Continue with Google as the alternative.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey authentication and registration as a first-class option while retaining accessible account recovery and existing fallbacks.

findings.summary: An unsolicited personalization sign-in promotion interrupts article reading before the user asks to personalize.
findings.evidence: The mobile article capture shows “Get the news, your way” as a centered modal over dimmed article content, with the already-large cookie decision surface still behind it.
findings.suggestedFix: Trigger personalization only after an explicit request or a non-blocking contextual cue, keep “Maybe later” equally prominent, and remember dismissal.

findings.summary: Several images are oversized or eagerly loaded below the fold.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 6 images over twice their displayed dimensions and 11 below-fold images without lazy loading. The HAR confirms modern WebP delivery for sampled large images, so format is not the concern.
findings.suggestedFix: Tighten responsive image candidate widths and lazy-load non-critical below-fold imagery while preserving eager loading and fetch priority for the LCP image.

findings.summary: The initial experience performs disproportionate background script and measurement work.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 67 scripts and multiple analytics origins; trace and layout evidence recorded repeated long tasks after content appeared.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load feature bundles, delay background measurement until idle and consent, and stop work when the page is hidden.

findings.summary: Repeated global-menu interaction correlates with substantial retained-heap growth and needs leak-trace confirmation.
findings.evidence: After ten menu open/escape cycles, the heap summary grew from 689,702 nodes / 38.9 MB self-size to 887,218 nodes / 52.2 MB. Separate page processes add noise, so this is a low-confidence leak signal, not a proven retained path.
findings.suggestedFix: Reproduce in one controlled baseline/target/final session, force collection between snapshots, and inspect retained paths for menu DOM, listeners, timers and caches before changing code.

taskList.title: Remove pre-consent tracking and minimize first-visit analytics
Reduce startup JavaScript and break up long main-thread tasks
Stop stacking first-visit consent and personalization interruptions
Respect dark mode and reduced-motion preferences
Use native dialog/popover primitives for overlays
Confirm or dismiss the repeated-menu heap-growth signal
Introduce preference-safe View Transitions for major state changes
